the synthesis of a series of novel multi-walled carbon nanostructures (MWCNs) and the study of the influence of these materials on the X-band electromagnetic absorption of their epoxy-based nanocomposites.
the synthesis and characterization of novel carbon nanomaterials, and the investigation of their potential for applications in nanoelectronics and energy conversion.
the development of a new class of materials for the microwave absorbers based on epoxy nanocomposites filled with different multi-walled CNTs.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have shown that the addition of MWCNTs to epoxy resin can significantly enhance the microwave absorption of the material.
the microwave absorption properties of epoxy-based nanocomposites are highly dependent on the type of carbon nanotube (CNT) used.
multi-walled carbon-nanotubes can be a good microwave absorber.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the microwave absorption properties of carbon nanotubes (CNTs) are highly dependent on the synthesis method, and the resulting structure of the CNTs, and that the microwave absorption of CNTs can be tuned by controlling the synthesis method.

the microwave properties of multi-walled carbon nano-tubes are highly dependent on their structure and that the absorption of the epoxy nanocomposites is highly dependent on the structure of their carbon nanotubes.
the microwave absorption properties of MWCNT-epoxy nanocomposites are highly dependent on MWCNT structure.
